title: Grade 9 Mathematics — Circles
description: Circles — chords, arcs, angles subtended, cyclic quadrilaterals (CBSE Ch. 10)
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The longest chord of a circle is:
questions.explanation: The diameter is the longest chord of a circle — it passes through the centre and its length is twice the radius.

questions.question: Equal chords of a circle subtend equal angles at the:
questions.explanation: Theorem: Equal chords of a circle (or congruent circles) subtend equal angles at the centre. This follows directly from congruent triangles formed by radii to the chord endpoints.

questions.question: The perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord:
questions.explanation: The perpendicular from the centre to any chord bisects it. This is a key theorem — the foot of the perpendicular is the midpoint of the chord.

questions.question: The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is _____ the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.
questions.explanation: Inscribed Angle Theorem: The angle subtended at the centre is double the angle subtended at any point on the remaining (major/minor) arc.

questions.question: Angles in the same segment of a circle are:
questions.explanation: Angles inscribed in the same arc (segment) of a circle are equal. Both look at the same chord from the same side.

questions.question: The angle in a semicircle is:
questions.explanation: The angle subtended by a diameter (semicircle) at the circumference is always 90° (Thales' theorem). The central angle for a diameter = 180°, so inscribed angle = 180°/2 = 90°.

questions.question: In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A + ∠C =
questions.explanation: In a cyclic quadrilateral (one inscribed in a circle), opposite angles are supplementary: ∠A + ∠C = 180° and ∠B + ∠D = 180°.

questions.question: In a circle, the central angle subtended by a chord AB is 80°. The inscribed angle subtended by the same chord on the major arc is:
questions.explanation: The inscribed angle = half the central angle. Central angle = 80°, so inscribed angle on the major arc = 80°/2 = 40°.

questions.question: Two circles of radii 5 cm and 3 cm intersect at two points. The distance between their centres is 4 cm. The length of the common chord is:
questions.explanation: Using the intersecting chords / coordinate approach: let centres be O₁O₂ = 4 cm, r₁ = 5, r₂ = 3. The common chord perpendicularly bisects the line joining centres. Solving: x = (16 + 25 − 9)/(2 × 4) = 4 from O₁, so half-chord = √(25 − 16) = 3, chord = 6 cm.

questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. If ∠A = 2x and ∠C = x + 30°, then x =
questions.explanation: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°: ∠A + ∠C = 180° → 2x + x + 30° = 180° → 3x = 150° → x = 50°.

questions.question: A chord of a circle is at a distance of 6 cm from the centre. The radius of the circle is 10 cm. The length of the chord is:
questions.explanation: Half-chord = √(r² − d²) = √(100 − 36) = √64 = 8 cm. Full chord = 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

questions.question: If two equal chords of a circle intersect within the circle, the segments of one chord are:
options: Equal to the corresponding segments of the other chord
Double the segments of the other
Half the segments of the other
questions.explanation: Theorem: If two equal chords of a circle intersect inside the circle, then the segments of one chord are equal respectively to the segments of the other chord.

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, ∠AOB = 100° where A and B are on the circle. The reflex ∠AOB is:
The angle subtended by a minor arc at the centre is 140°. The angle subtended by the major arc at a point on the minor arc is:
questions.explanation: The major arc subtends a central angle of 360° − 140° = 220°. By the inscribed angle theorem, the angle at a point on the minor arc (looking at the major arc) = 220°/2 = 110°.

questions.question: How many circles can be drawn through three non-collinear points?
questions.explanation: Through any three non-collinear points, exactly one unique circle can be drawn. (If the points were collinear, no circle could pass through all three.)
